To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a taxonomy of attacks on cloud computing based on the notion that an attacker exploits the attack surfaces of the various cloud computing participants, i.e., the attacker targets the cloud service, its data or its users.
the taxonomy of attacks on the cloud is based on the notion and classification of attack surfaces of cloud computing participants.

the cloud scenario can be modeled as a system of systems, that the cloud scenario is characterized by a high degree of heterogeneity, and that the cloud computing scenario has a high degree of interdependency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the different attack surface components of a cloud service.
(1) identifying the attack surfaces of the participants in the cloud computing scenario and (2) developing appropriate classification criteria for attacks that target these surfaces.

the following questions: What are the different types of attacks on cloud computing? What are the main security risks that cloud computing poses? Which are the most critical attack surfaces in the context of cloud computing? What is the impact of cloud computing on existing attacks and security mechanisms?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the attack surface of a participant of the cloud computing paradigm is a function of the participant’s role and its interactions with the other participants.
the taxonomy is a work-in-progress.
the cloud computing scenario is characterized by the presence of a number of attack surfaces, each of which can be targeted by an adversary.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the attack surface is a set of all the possible attack vectors for the cloud computing participants.
the attack surfaces are the interfaces of the cloud computing participants that can be used by an attacker in order to compromise the security of the cloud computing environment.
the attack surface of a cloud service is the sum of the attack surfaces of all the participants in a cloud service.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cloud computing attack surface is a complex entity, which consists of the attack surfaces of all the participants of a cloud service.
a comprehensive taxonomy should be based on the notion that the attack surface of a participant is not a static entity but rather a dynamic one that depends on the context of the attack.
the attack surface of a cloud participant is the sum of the attack surfaces of its sub-participants.
